text:
kai: Heads-up — onboarding a community mixtral dump (mixtral-7b-sft.safetensors) and seeing a 2.5x tail latency regression on the staged canary. TL;DR: kernel selector falling back to generic_gemm for the first ~20 tokens, batcher starts thrashing and KV hit ratio drops.
sara: Ugh. Any obvious parsing errors from HF config or safetensors metadata?
chris: I grabbed the artifact and ran the parser locally. HF config is missing `num_attention_heads` in the json (model config has `n_head` under a nested legacy key). Our hf-parse assumed `num_attention_heads` or `n_head` at top-level; fallback path returns null and kernel chooser thinks it's an atypical layout so picks generic kernels.
kai: That explains the kernel choice. Perf numbers from the canary: median token latency ~8ms -> 9ms (fine) but p99 jumped 8ms -> 24ms. Throughput down ~18%.
sara: Can you paste the snippet that shows where we bail to generic? The selector logic is in runtime/kernel_selector.cc right?
chris: Yeah, here's the log from the staged server: ```[kernel-selector] model_id=mixtral-7b-sft parsed_heads=null inferred_heads=32 kernel=generic_gemm reason="missing explicit heads metadata"```
nina: If parsed_heads is null we should attempt the legacy keys before giving up. Quick patch idea: try `n_head`, `num_heads`, and `attn_heads`. Also add a safety heuristic: if heads missing but weight shapes match (qkv shape divisible by 3*head_size), infer heads and continue.
kai: Agreed. But we also need to reduce batcher thrash while we fix parse logic. Right now batches are size-1 for many requests until KV warms up. Any quick batching heuristics we can enable?
sara: We can enable a short-lived hysteresis window: if a model's kernel falls back unexpectedly, allow the batcher to wait 20ms for a second request before flushing. That prevents immediate single-token flushes. I'll open a flag: `batcher.delay_on_kernel_fallback_ms` default 0 -> 20 for canary.
chris: I pushed two small diffs. One fixes parser lookup order and adds inference-from-weight fallback (see PR: https://git.redwood/repo/pull/3421). Second toggles the batcher hysteresis flag in the canary config (https://git.redwood/repo/pull/3423).
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary cluster (namespace: eng-runtime-canary) — rolling 3 nodes, 30s interval. Link: https://deploys.redwood/eng-runtime-canary/7842
nina: Also worth checking safetensors metadata — some exported safetensors drop axis names. I ran `safetensors inspect` and got: ```tensor q_proj: shape=(32, 3072) metadata={} ``` No axis info to know head dim. Our converter should annotate with `heads` and `kv_head_dim` when available. I'll add that to the conversion script.
kai: Good. If the parser fallback works, we should see the kernel switch back to optimized attention kernels. What's our validated way to infer heads from weights? Any pitfalls?
chris: Heuristic: qkv weight shape is (embed_dim, 3*embed_dim) OR (embed_dim, 3*head_dim*heads). We compute head_dim = (qkv_cols / 3) / guessed_heads. If head_dim integer and head_dim * heads == embed_dim/?? — it's messy but reliable for most models. I'll add unit tests using known models (llama, qwen, mixtral) to avoid false inferences.
sara: After deploy I'll run the perf profiler against the canary for 1h and share flamegraphs. If tail latency drops near previous baseline we merge. If not, we revert and triage deeper.
kai: Perf thresholds for auto-merge: p99 <= 12ms, throughput within 95% of baseline. Otherwise revert. Sound good?
nina: Sounds good. I also added a small conversion fix (line in converter): ```if not metadata.get('heads'): metadata['heads']=inferred_heads; write_metadata(tensor, metadata)``` This will help future exports.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy completed (3/3). Rollout id: r-2026-11-03-7842.
chris: Early profiling (10m): p99 down to 11ms, throughput -2%. KV hit ratio back to normal after warm-up. Flamegraph: kernel time moved from generic_gemm -> optimized_local_attention. Link: https://profiles.redwood/eng-runtime/7842/trace
kai: Nice. Let's keep the canary up for 24h, then promote to staging if stable. Also file a follow-up to add better safetensors annotation guidance in the docs (devex ticket).
sara: Creating the devex ticket now: https://tickets.redwood/DEVEX-809. Will include converter snippet and recommended exporter flags.
nina: I'll open a small telemetry alert to catch missing heads metadata in new model uploads — fires when parsed_heads is null for >3 unique models in 24h.
kai: Thanks all. Summary: parser fallback fix + converter metadata write + batcher hysteresis got canary back to baseline. Hold canary 24h and watch alerts. :thumbsup:
